title: 2013 AMC 10A 18
statement: Let points \(A=(0,0),\) \(B=(1,2),\) \(C=(3,3),\) and \(D=(4,0).\) Quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is cut into equal area pieces by a line passing through \(A.\) This line intersects \(\overline{CD}\) at point \(\left(\dfrac{p}{q}, \dfrac{r}{s}\right),\) where these fractions are in lowest terms. What is \(p+q+r+s?\)

solutions.text:
Let the cutting line meet \(\overline{CD}\) at \(G\). Drop perpendiculars from \(B\), \(C\), and \(G\) to the \(x\)-axis as in the diagram.

The areas of \(\triangle ABF\), trapezoid \(BCEF\), and \(\triangle CDE\) are \(1\), \(5\), and \(\frac32\), respectively, so \([ABCD]=\frac{15}{2}\).

Thus \(\triangle ADG\) has area \(\frac{15}{4}\). Since \(AD=4\), the height of \(G\) is \(\frac{15}{8}\).

The line \(CD\) has equation \(y=-3x+12\), so \(\frac{15}{8}=-3x+12\), giving \(x=\frac{27}{8}\). Therefore \(p+q+r+s\) \(=27+8+15+8\) \(=58\).

Thus, B is the correct answer.
hints: First compute the total area of \(ABCD\)
The cutting line through \(A\) makes \(\triangle ADG\) half the quadrilateral area
